name: ENCOM Program Arena
backstory: Three embodied programs divide agile contact, measured fire and cautious support. The arena gives each avatar one ordinary equipment plan without turning software identity into extra mechanics.
strategy_personality: An embodied-software collection: luminous circuit suits, strong disc silhouettes, and distinct source costumes. These are computer programs represented by human-like avatars; placing them in a physical robot arena is an explicit Armoured Souls adaptation. Preserve the original avatars instead of inventing mechanical faces. The three form a proposed arena collection across opposing sides. Do not add Rinzler as a fourth independent character alongside Tron.

robots.name: Tron
robots.art_brief:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: Armoured Souls individual robot game portrait. Generate ONE square 1:1 image of ONE complete source-faithful robot, not an original substitute.
Scene/backdrop: quiet charcoal-to-black industrial studio gradient, subtle dark floor and restrained low haze.
Style/medium: premium realistic industrial sci-fi hard-surface 3D rendering, believable metal, fine scratches and restrained paint wear, preserving source geometry and colours. Match the established Armoured Souls portrait collection.
Composition: three-quarter view, complete full body with head, all feet/legs and equipment contained in frame, centered at about 80% of square canvas with at least 5% clear margin around every extremity. Readable silhouette at 512px.
Lighting: neutral soft key, cool upper-right rim light, controlled cinematic contrast and subtle source-appropriate sensors.
Constraints: one character, no additional figures, no collage/grid, no text/captions, watermark, UI or border, no firing or explosions. Keep canonical proportions and anatomy; do not add humanoid arms to walkers or astromechs. Full-resolution square master for 512x512 WebP export.

Subject: Tron from TRON 1982, human-looking male program avatar with original white/grey circuit suit, blue glowing circuit lines, original rounded helmet, black undersuit details and identity disc carried low in one hand. Original 1982 face and suit geometry, not TRON Legacy's black suit. Full body, no invented mechanical face.
Metadata only, do not render text: #168 slot 1 Tron.
robots.refinement_note: Trio follows the supplied strategy rule: no weapon refinements. This is an explicit empty plan.
robots.equipment_interpretation: Tron fills the agile contact specialist role. Its source body and selected portrait are retained. Arena main/offhand allocations can use fitted mounts or tool adapters; extra limbs, integrated source weapons and alternate forms grant no additional slots or combat effects.
robots.combat_rationale: Sprinter tuning supports the melee equipment role; offensive stance and a 10% yield threshold implement its pressure or survival priority. Range follows the equipped weapons at both stages.
robots.tuning_plan: Use the existing Trio strategy tuning rules with the Sprinter Build_Focus and its free pool; equipment refinements do not replace robot tuning.
robots.design_basis: New arena build authored for this collection using supplied equipment prices, hand compatibility and verified refinement examples. Original source identity and final artwork remain authoritative for appearance.
